## RUL Calculation Demo

**RUL (Remaining Useful Life)** is the number of cycles before an engine fails.

```{webr-r}
# Define engine lifecycle
max_cycle <- 200
current_cycle <- 150

# Calculate RUL
RUL <- max_cycle - current_cycle

cat("Engine Status Report\n")
cat("====================\n")
cat("Max Lifecycle:", max_cycle, "cycles\n")
cat("Current Cycle:", current_cycle, "\n")
cat("RUL:", RUL, "cycles remaining\n")
```

**Try it:** Change `current_cycle` to different values and re-run!

---

## Maintenance Decision Logic

Based on RUL, we make maintenance decisions:

```{webr-r}
# Try changing this value: 25, 45, or 80
RUL <- 50

# Maintenance decision logic
if (RUL < 30) {
  cat("CRITICAL: Schedule maintenance NOW!\n")
  cat("Risk Level: HIGH")
} else if (RUL < 50) {
  cat("WARNING: Plan maintenance soon\n")
  cat("Risk Level: MEDIUM")
} else {
  cat("HEALTHY: Engine is safe\n")
  cat("Risk Level: LOW")
}
```

## Sensor Degradation Simulation

Engines degrade over time. Sensor 11 (pressure) shows the "Death Signature":

```{webr-r}
# Simulate sensor behavior over 200 cycles
set.seed(42)
cycles <- 1:200

# Healthy phase (flat) + Degradation phase (exponential rise)
healthy <- rep(550, 150) + rnorm(150, 0, 5)
degradation <- 550 + exp(seq(0, 3, length.out = 50)) * 10
sensor_11 <- c(healthy, degradation)

# Summary statistics
cat("Sensor 11 Analysis\n")
cat("==================\n")
cat("Start value:", round(sensor_11[1], 1), "psi\n")
cat("End value:", round(sensor_11[200], 1), "psi\n")
cat("Total increase:", round(sensor_11[200] - sensor_11[1], 1), "psi\n")
cat("\nThis exponential rise is the 'Death Signature'!")
```

---

## Visualizing the Death Signature

Let's plot the sensor degradation:

```{webr-r}
# Simulate sensor data
set.seed(42)
healthy <- rep(550, 150) + rnorm(150, 0, 5)
degradation <- 550 + exp(seq(0, 3, length.out = 50)) * 10
sensor_11 <- c(healthy, degradation)

# Create a simple plot
plot(1:200, sensor_11, type = "l", col = "red", lwd = 2,
     main = "Sensor 11: The Death Signature",
     xlab = "Cycle", ylab = "Pressure (psi)")
abline(v = 150, col = "blue", lty = 2)
text(130, 700, "Degradation\nStarts", col = "blue")
```

## Feature Engineering: Rolling Statistics

We use rolling windows to smooth sensor noise:

```{webr-r}
# Sample sensor data (noisy)
sensor_raw <- c(550, 548, 555, 552, 560, 558, 570, 575, 590, 620)

# Calculate rolling mean (window = 3)
rolling_mean <- function(x, k = 3) {
  n <- length(x)
  result <- rep(NA, n)
  for (i in k:n) {
    result[i] <- mean(x[(i - k + 1):i])
  }
  result
}

smoothed <- rolling_mean(sensor_raw, 3)

cat("Raw vs Smoothed Data\n")
cat("====================\n")
cat("Raw:     ", paste(sensor_raw, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Smoothed:", paste(round(smoothed, 1), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("\nRolling mean reduces noise and reveals trends!")
```

## RUL Clipping Technique

Industry standard: Cap RUL at 125 cycles to reduce noise:

```{webr-r}
# Raw RUL values (some very high)
raw_RUL <- c(250, 180, 125, 80, 50, 30, 10, 0)

# Apply clipping
clipped_RUL <- pmin(raw_RUL, 125)

cat("RUL Clipping Demo\n")
cat("=================\n")
for (i in 1:length(raw_RUL)) {
  cat("Raw:", raw_RUL[i], "-> Clipped:", clipped_RUL[i], "\n")
}
cat("\nWhy? When RUL > 125, sensors are flat (healthy).\n")
cat("Training on these 'boring' samples adds noise.")
```

## RMSE Calculation

**Root Mean Square Error** measures prediction accuracy:

```{webr-r}
# True RUL vs Predicted RUL for 5 engines
true_RUL <- c(50, 80, 120, 30, 95)
pred_RUL <- c(55, 75, 115, 40, 90)

# Calculate RMSE
errors <- true_RUL - pred_RUL
squared_errors <- errors ^ 2
mse <- mean(squared_errors)
rmse <- sqrt(mse)

cat("RMSE Calculation\n")
cat("================\n")
cat("True RUL: ", paste(true_RUL, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Pred RUL: ", paste(pred_RUL, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Errors:   ", paste(errors, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("\nRMSE =", round(rmse, 2), "cycles\n")
cat("Interpretation: On average, we predict within", round(rmse, 1), "cycles of truth")
```

## Try Your Own Analysis!

Modify and run this template:

```{webr-r}
# YOUR PLAYGROUND - modify freely!

# Create some engine data
engines <- c("Engine_A", "Engine_B", "Engine_C")
current_cycles <- c(150, 80, 195)
max_cycles <- c(200, 200, 200)

# Calculate RUL for each
for (i in 1:3) {
  RUL <- max_cycles[i] - current_cycles[i]
  status <- ifelse(RUL < 30, "CRITICAL",
            ifelse(RUL < 50, "WARNING", "HEALTHY"))
  cat(engines[i], "- RUL:", RUL, "cycles -", status, "\n")
}
```
